la:noun:sacerdos.html:
săcerdos, ōtis, comm. (
fem. collat. form SACERDOTA, ; cf. antistes init.; gen. plur. SACERDOTIVM, ) [sacer], a priest; a priestess: divis aliis alii sacerdotes, omnibus pontifices, singulis flamines sunto. . . sacerdotum duo genera sunto: unum quod praesit caerimoniis et sacris, alterum quod interpretetur fatidicorum et vatum effata incognita, etc.,; cf. ; : in collegio sacerdotum,: publici,; ; ; : Phoebi,: sacerdotes casti,: populi Romani,: Jovis,; cf. Dialis,: Dianae Ephesiae,: maximus (Syracusanorum),: tumuloque sacerdos additur Anchiseo,.—In fem.: sacra Cereris per Graecas semper curata sunt sacerdotes, etc.,; : Veneris,; cf. Veneria,; 2, 3, 20; 3, 2, 30: hujus fani,.—Absol., ; ; : Vestae,a Vestal,; (37): Vestalis, an old formula ap. : Troïa,i. e. Ilia, et saep.; v. the inscriptions in Orell. 2160 sq.—In apposition: proximi nobilissimis ac sacerdotibus viris,: in illo adultero sacerdote,: sacerdotem anum praecipem Reppulit,; cf. regina (i. e. Rhea Silvia),.— Transf., sarcastically: ille popularis, i. e. Clodius (on account of his smuggling himself in among the priestesses of the Bona Dea),; of the same: stuprorum sacerdos,: tyranni sacerdos,.—In eccl. Lat., of Christ as a mediator between God and men, .

la:adj:sacer.gloss: sacred, holy, dedicated (to a divinity), consecrated, hallowed (translating Greek ἱερός)
senses: sacred, holy, dedicated (to a divinity), consecrated, hallowed (translating Greek ἱερός)
devoted (to a divinity for sacrifice), fated (to destruction), forfeited, accursed
divine, celestial
execrable, detestable, horrible, infamous; criminal, impious, wicked, abominable, cursed
la:adj:sacer.html:
săcer, să_cra, să_crum (ante-class. collat. form sacer, sacris, sacre; plur.:
sacres porci,; ; ; ; sing. acc.: sacrem porcum, Fest. s. h. v. p. 318 Müll.), adj.
root sa-; Gr. σάος, σῶος, safe; whence Lat. sānus
, dedicated or consecrated to a divinity, holy, sacred, = ἱερός (cf.: sanctus, augustus): Gallus Aelius ait, sacrum esse quocumque modo atque instituto civitatis consecratum sit, sive aedis, sive ara, sive signum, sive locus, sive pecunia, sive quid aliud quod dis dedicatum atque consecratum sit, Fest. s. v. sacer mons, p. 318 Müll.; cf.: quicquid destinatum est diis, sacrum vocatur,: sacrae (res) sunt quae diis superis consecratae sunt: religiosae quae diis manibus relictae sunt,.
In gen.
Absol.: quicquam (opp. profanum),; ; cf.: aedificiis omnibus, publicis privatis sacris profanis, sic pepercit, etc.,; so, locus sacer et profanus,; ; : miscebis sacra profanis,; ; ; : villae signis et tabulis refertae partim publicis partim etiam sacris et religiosis,; so (with religiosus) ; : mores autem rapere properant quā sacrum quā puplicum,: (legum) genera sunt tria, sacri, publici, privati juris,; cf. in the sup.: deprecor hoc unum per jura sacerrima lecti,: aedes,; ; ; : lucus late sacer,: arvum Martis,: ara,: aurum,; cf. pecunia (opp. privata),: arma,: tus,: sanguis (of the sacrificial victim),: ales (so called from its use in augury),: luces (with profestae),; cf. dies (with religiosus),: tempus,: commissum,a crime against religion, et saep.— Poet.: vitis (as sacred to Bacchus), Enn. ap. P. (Trag. v. 149 Vahl.); ; so, laurus,; : robur,: aqua,: fontes,; : focus,: Tarentum,: fines,; cf. montes (the Alps, because not to be ascended by men),; vates (because dedicated to Apollo),; ; cf.: sacer interpresque deorum Orpheus,; and (for sanctus) of the divinity itself: Vesta, (4, 3), 11; so, Cybebe, (but in : ut sacrosancti habeantur, quibus ipsi dii neque sacri neque sancti sunt, so used only on account of the lusus verbb. with sacrosancti; v. the context).—Sacer Mons,a hill about three miles from Rome, beyond the Anio, and on the right of the Via Nomentana, to which the Roman people retired during their controversy with the Senate,; ; ; : os sacrum, quod imum ventrem sustinet,: Sacra Via, or (poet.) Sacer Clivus, a street in Rome leading from the Forum to the Capitol, ; ; ; ; ; v. also via, I. A. 2.: sacer morbus,the epilepsy,: sacer lapis,a stone landmark, a mere-stone,: os sacrum, anatom. t. t., = Gr. ἱερὸν ὀστέον,the lowest bone of the spine, : litterae sacrae (eccl. Lat.),the Scriptures,.—For its combinations with ignis, via, etc., v. those words.—
With gen. (class.): ego te sacram coronam surripuisse scio Jovis,; so, urna Veneris, (for which: urna Veneria,): Dianae celebris dies,: sepulcrum Batti veteris,; cf. .—As a predicate: terra, ut focus domiciliorum, sacra deorum omnium est (a transl. of the Platon. Γῆ ἱερὰ πάντων θεῶν), , 18, 45: illa insula (sc. Delos) eorum deorum sacra putatur,.—
With dat. (mostly poet. and in post-Aug. prose; cf. infra, II. A.): sacra Jovi quercus,: esculus Jovi sacra,: Nymphis cervus,: Cereri Polyphoetes (as a priest),: pugionem templo Salutis detraxerat gestabatque velut magno operi sacrum,: cupressus Diti sacra,: aesculus Jovi,.—As a predicate: Jani mensis, Qui sacer est imis Manibus,, quercus antiqua, quae erat Marti sacra, (al. sacrata).—
Transf., in gen., holy, sacred, awful, venerable (not till after the Aug. per., and very rare): silentium,: laedere amantes, (4, 15), 11: lingua (Ciceronis),: Maro, id. 8. 56, 3: quaedam patris memoria,: O sacer et magnus vatum labor,: heu sacri vatum errores,.—So used of the emperors; disapproved of by Tiberius: (Tiberius) alium dicentem sacras ejus occupationes verba mutare et pro sacris laboriosas dicere coëgit,.—But soon after Tiberius in general use: auris Caesaris,: sacri lateris custos,: apud aures sacras mentitus est, (cf.: se Imperatori mentitum,); and hence, for ecclesiastical: domus, comitatus, scrinia, largitiones, etc., in the law books et saep.
In partic., with a bad accessory signif., devoted to a divinity for destruction, forfeited; and absol., accursed, criminal, impious, wicked.
With dat.: si quisquam aliuta faxit, ipsos Jovi sacer esto, Lex Numae ap. Müll.; cf.: ut caput ejus Jovi sacrum esset, an ancient plebiscitum ap. : non alienum videtur, de condicione eorum hominum referre, quos leges sacros esse certis diis jubent, quod, cum cetera sacra violari nefas sit, hominem sacrum jus fuerit occidi, etc.,.—
Absol.: homo sacer is est, quem populus judicavit ob maleficium; neque fas est eum immolari; sed qui occidit, parricidii non damnatur. Nam lege tribuniciā primā cavetur: si quis eum, qui eo plebei scito sacer sit, occiderit, parricida ne sit. Ex quo quivis homo malus atque improbus sacer appellari solet, Fest. s. v. sacer mons, p. 318 Müll.: PATRONVS SI CLIENTI FRAVDEM FECERIT SACER ESTO, LEX XII. Tab. ap. ; in imitation: uter aedilis fuerit, etc. ... is intestabilis et sacer esto,: eum, qui cuiquam nocuerit, sacrum sanciri,.—
Transf., in gen., accursed, execrable, detestable, horrible, infamous, etc. (only poet. and in post-Aug. prose).
Of persons: ego sum malus, Ego sum sacer, scelestus,; Afran. ap. (with malus); .—Sup., : homo sacerrimus,; ; Turp. ap. (with pessimus). —
Of things: sacerrimum domicilium, Turp. ap. : di magni, horribilem et sacrum libellum,: hircus alarum,: auri fames, (for which: aurum fame,: venenum (Medeae),: nox,: arma metu,; cf. pavor,: insania,: morbus,i. e. epilepsy,.—With dat.: ut immerentis fluxit in terram Remi Sacer nepotibus cruor,.— Comp. and adv. do not appear (as for the comp. v. Müll.).—Hence, subst.: să_crum, i, n., something consecrated; a holy or sacred thing, a sacred vessel or utensil; a sanctuary, a temple; a religious act, a sacrifice, etc.; in plur. in gen., sacred rites, religious worship, religion (both of the State and of single races and families; and even of individuals; v.infra, β; class.; most freq. in plur.).
Lit.
Sing.: sacrum sacrove commendatum qui cleperit rapsitque parricida esto,: ubi sacro manus sis admolitus,: omne sacrum rapiente dextrā,: metuens velut contingere sacrum,: apud Cluacinae sacrum,; : Minervae,: theatrum veluti quoddam illius sacri templum vocabimus,:

quae (sacerdos Cereris) Graecum illud sacrum monstraret et faceret, : sacrum Herculi facere,: facere Junoni,facto per Magos sacro,: sollemne sacrum conficere,: ita se habet sacrum (Suovetaurilia),: arma lecta conici in acervum jussit consul sacrumque id Vulcano cremavit,: sacrum piaculare fieri,: sollemne Apollinis sacrum,; : pyrā sacri sub imagine factā,: nec de lucernā fas est accendi sacrum,: neve initianto, nisi ut assolet, Cereri, Graeco sacro,according to the Grecian rites,; cf.: vetabo, qui Cereris sacrum Vulgarit arcanae,: morientibus operire (oculos) rursusque in rogo patefacere, Quiritium ritu sacrum est,: in sacro est,.—

Plur.: sacra deosque penates .. ex aedibus suis eripuisse dixit, sacred vessels or utensils, holy things, ; cf. : sacra omnia proferre, Auct. B. Alex. 32, 3: portabant canistris,: Troïa,: velut qui Junonis sacra ferret,; cf. of the same,; Heyne; ; ; : cumque suis penetralia sacris,i. e. the images of the gods, Penates,: jactata aequoribus sacra,: pueri Sacra canunt,sacred songs,; cf. : sacra ordine in mensā Penatium deorum Ponuntur,sacred gifts, offerings,: neve ulla vitiorum sacra sollemnia obeunto,: sicut in sollemnibus sacris fieri consuevit,: qui (Mercurius) sacris anniversariis coleretur, (for which: sacrificiis anniversariis colebatur,, § 128: sacris e principum numero pontifices quinque praefecit,: (Romulus) sacra diis aliis Albano ritu, Graeco Herculi facit,; cf.: sacra Jovi facturus erat,: sacra Jovi Stygio Perficere,: ipse (Numa) plurima sacra obibat,: densi circumstant sacra ministri,: arcana sacra,; : fera,: nefanda,: mystica,: horrida,: veneranda,: casta,.
Divine worship or religion in gen.: publica sacra, quae publico sumptu pro populo fiunt, quaeque pro montibus, pagis, curiis, sacellis: at privata, quae pro singulis hominibus, familiis, gentibus fiunt, Fest. pp. 244 and 245 Müll.; : quo foedere (Romulus) et Sabinos in civitatem ascivit, sacris communicatis,: quod per populum errari fas non erat propter religionem sacrorum,; so, religio sacrorum,: sacra Cereris conficere,; so, Cereris, (cf. supra, αfin.): Eleusina,: Junonis,: Orphica,rites, solemnity, festival,: Bacchia,: trieterica Bacchi,: Dianae,; 15, 489: Isidis, et saep.—
The private religious rites of a gens, a family, etc. (observed by the Romans with the greatest care): sacra privata perpetua manento,; cf. : an gentilicia sacra ne in bello quidem intermitti, publica sacra et Romanos deos etiam in pace deseri placet?: ut ne morte patris familias sacrorum memoria occideret,: docebant (antiqui) tribus modis sacris adstringi,: magnum est eadem habere monumenta majorum, eisdem uti sacris, sepulcra habere communia,; cf.: ut qui natus sit, ignoret, cujus sanguinis, quorum sacrorum sit,: sacra interire illi (majores) noluerunt,: sacrorum alienatio, (v. alienatio); cf. sing.: sacrum familiare,: nuptialia,marriage solemnities,; called also jugalia,; cf. respecting the sacra privata of the Romans, Savigny, in his Zeitschr. 2, p. 397 sq.—
Poet., poems (as sacred to the Muses): mihi jam puero caelestia sacra placebant, Inque suum furtim Musa trahebat opus,: vatum,: Maronis,. —
Prov.
Inter sacrum saxumque stare, to stand between the victim and the knife, i. e. to be between the door and the wall, to be in great straits, ; cf.: inter sacrum et saxum positus,—
Hereditas sine sacris, i. e. a great profit without trouble, = a rose without thorns, meat without bone, etc. (because the keeping up of the sacra privata was attended with great expense), , and ; cf. Müll.—
Transf., in gen. (the figure being borrowed from secret religious rites), in plur.: sacra, secrets, mysteries (not till after the Aug. period, and very rare): sacra tori coitusque novos referebam,: peregisse mihi videor sacra tradentium artes, (cf.: omnes fere, qui legem dicendi, quasi quaedam mysteria, tradiderunt,): litterarum colere,: studiorum profanare,.

la:verb:sacro.gloss: to declare or set apart as sacred; consecrate, dedicate, hallow or devote; sanctify, enshrine
senses: to declare or set apart as sacred; consecrate, dedicate, hallow or devote; sanctify, enshrine
to doom or devote to destruction, declare accursed, condemn
to hold, worship or honor as sacred
to render imperishable, deify, immortalize
la:verb:sacro.html:
să_cro, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.
sacer
,
to declare or set apart as sacred; to consecrate, dedicate, or devote to a divinity (class.; cf. consecro).
Lit.: ne quis agrum consecrato. Auri, argenti, eboris sacrandi modus esto,: eum praedam Veientanam publicando sacrandoque ad nihilum redegisse, ferociter increpant,: (agrum) Cypriae,: Capitolino Jovi donum ex auro,: (laurum) Phoebo,: aras,: vigilem ignem,: votum immortale,: inter haec auream aquilam pinnis extendenti similem sacraverant,: templum, in quo Helena sacravit calicem ex electro,.—In part. perf.: duabus aris ibi Jovi et Soli sacratis cum immolasset,: arae,: sacratas fide manus,: sacrata Crotonis Ossa tegebat humus,: rite pecudes,: templum, al. —
With a bad accessory signif. (cf. sacer, II.), to devote or doom to destruction, to declare accursed, to condemn: de sacrando cum bonis capite ejus, qui regni occupandi consilia inisset, gratae in vulgus leges fuere,; cf.: caput Jovi,.—
Transf., in gen., to set apart, consecrate, devote, give, dedicate a thing to any one (poet. and rare): quod patriae vocis studiis nobisque sacrasti, Cic. poët. Div. 1, 13, 22: hunc illi honorem Juppiter sacravit,: tibi sacratum opus,.—In a bad sense: injecere manum Parcae, telisque sacrarunt Evandri (Halaesum),.—
Meton.
To render sacred or inviolable by consecration; to hallow, consecrale: hoc nemus aeterno cinerum sacravit honore Faenius,: foedus, quod in Capitolio sacratum fuisset, irritum per illos esse,that had been decreed inviolable,; cf.: sanctiones sacrandae sunt genere ipso aut obtestatione legis, aut, etc.,, 33: sacrata lex,a law whose violation was punished by devoting the offender to the infernal gods,; ; ; ; ; 9, 39; 36, 38; cf.: sacratae leges sunt, quibus sanctum est, qui quid adversus eas fecerit, sacer alicui deorum sit cum familia pecuniaque, Müll.—
Of a deity, to hold sacred, to worship or honor as sacred: haud frustra te patrem deum hominumque hac sede sacravimus,: Vesta sacrata,.—
Transf., in gen., to render imperishable, to immortalize (rare): aliquem Lesbio plectro,; cf.: miratur nihil, nisi quod Libitina sacravit,: vivit vigetque eloquentia ejus (Catonis), sacrata scriptis omnis generis,: avum Sacrārunt carmina tuum,.—Hence, să_crātus, a, um, P. a., hallowed, consecrated, holy, sacred: sacrata jura parentum,: jura Graiorum,: vittae Sacrati capitis,: dux,i. e. Augustus,; cf.: manus (Tiberii),: dies sacratior,: numen gentibus sacratissimum,: homines,devoted to the gods,; , 2, 26.—At a later per., Sacratissimus,an epithet of the emperors, Most Worshipful,; et saep.—Adv.: să_-crātē, in eccl. Lat.,
Holily, piously: vivere,—
Mysteriously, mystically, .

Alex. 32, 3: portabant canistris,: Troïa,: velut qui Junonis sacra ferret,; cf. of the same,; Heyne; ; ; : cumque suis penetralia sacris,i. e. the images of the gods, Penates,: jactata aequoribus sacra,: pueri Sacra canunt,sacred songs,; cf. : sacra ordine in mensā Penatium deorum Ponuntur,sacred gifts, offerings,: neve ulla vitiorum sacra sollemnia obeunto,: sicut in sollemnibus sacris fieri consuevit,: qui (Mercurius) sacris anniversariis coleretur, (for which: sacrificiis anniversariis colebatur,, § 128: sacris e principum numero pontifices quinque praefecit,: (Romulus) sacra diis aliis Albano ritu, Graeco Herculi facit,; cf.: sacra Jovi facturus erat,: sacra Jovi Stygio Perficere,: ipse (Numa) plurima sacra obibat,: densi circumstant sacra ministri,: arcana sacra,; : fera,: nefanda,: mystica,: horrida,: veneranda,: casta,.

Prov.
Inter sacrum saxumque stare, to stand between the victim and the knife, i. e. to be between the door and the wall, to be in great straits, ; cf.: inter sacrum et saxum positus,—
Hereditas sine sacris, i. e. a great profit without trouble, = a rose without thorns, meat without bone, etc. (because the keeping up of the sacra privata was attended with great expense), , and ; cf. Müll.—

la:noun:sacramentum.gloss: a sum of money deposited in pledge by two individuals involved in a suit, the money of the loser in the suit being used for religious purposes
senses: a sum of money deposited in pledge by two individuals involved in a suit, the money of the loser in the suit being used for religious purposes
sacrament (an oath of allegiance)
sacrament (sacred act and the attendant ceremony, considered an outward sign of divine grace, instituted by Jesus Christ)
a mystery, secret
la:noun:sacramentum.html:
să_crāmentum, i, n.
sacro
.
In good class. Lat., a jurid. and milit. t. t.
Jurid. t. t., the sum which the two parties to a suit at first deposited, but afterwards became bound for, with the tresviri capitales; so called because the sum deposited by the losing party was used for religious purposes, esp. for the sacra publica; v. Müll.; or, perh. more correctly, because the money was deposited in a sacred place; v.the foll. passage of Varro and Müller's note. (Another reason is given in : sacramentum est pignus sponsionis; vocatum autem sacramentum, quia violare, quod quisque promittit, perfidia est): ea pecunia, quae in judicium venit in litibus, sacramentum a sacro. Qui petebat et qui infitiabatur, de aliis rebus utrique quingenos aeris ad pontem deponebant, de aliis rebus item certo alio legitimo numero assum; qui judicio vicerat, suom sacramentum e sacro auferebat, victi ad aerarium redibat, Müll. N. cr.: qui prior vindicaverat, dicebat: quando tu injuria vindicavisti, de aeris sacramento te provoco; adversarius quoque dicebat: similiter ego te; seu L. asses sacramenti nominabant... Postea praedes Praetor ab utroque accipiebat sacramenti, quod id in publicum cedebat,; cf. , § 13 sq.; 95: sacramenti autem nomine id aes dici coeptum est quod et propter aerarii inopiam et sacrorum publicorum multitudinem consumebatur id in rebus divinis, Müll.: cum in rem aliquam agerent litigatores et poena se sacramenti peterent, poscebant judicem, qui dabatur post trigesimum diem, Pseudo-Ascon. ad. (p. 164 Orell.): de multae sacramento consules comitiis centuriatis tulerunt,.—
Meton., a cause, a civil suit or process: decemviri re quaesitā et deliberatā sacramentum nostrum justum judicaverunt,; cf. transf. in gen.: homines graves, quibuscum tibi justo sacramento contendere, non liceret,on equal terms, with a fair chance of success,: cetera ... ἔντεχνα et arguta adparebunt, ut sacramento contendas mea non esse, lay a wager, i. e. confidently assert, : injustis vindiciis ac sacramentis ali enos fundos petere,: si Xviri

sacramentum in libertatem injustum judicassent, .—

Milit. t. t. (cf. infra, 2, the passage from ), orig. the preliminary engagement entered into by newly-enlisted troops (this was followed by the proper military oath, jusjurandum, which was at first voluntary, but, after the second Punic war, was demanded by the military tribune): milites tum (i.e. 538 A.U.C.), quod numquam antea factum erat, jurejurando ab tribunis militum adacti milites [jussu consulis conventuros]: nam ad eam diem nihil praeter sacramentum fuerat; et, ubi ad decuriatum aut centuriatum convenissent, suā voluntate ipsi inter sese decuriati equites, centuriati pedites conjurabant, sese fugae atque formidinis ergo non abituros neque ex ordine recessuros, nisi, etc.... Id ex voluntario inter ipsos foedere ad tribunos ac legitimam juris jurandi adactionem translatum, seq. Weissenb. ad loc.; cf. ; and v. Becker, Antiq. 3, 2, p. 292 sq.—Hence, since that time,
For jusjurandum, the military oath of allegiance (very freq. and class.): milites Domitianos sacramentum apud se dicere jubet,to take the oath of allegiance,; so, sacramentum dicere,fin.: quos consulis sacramento rogavisset,: sacramentum dicere alicui,; and in a like signif. in Livy: sacramento (abl.) dicere, ; ; ; 41, 5 fin.: sacramento dicere alicui,: ut omnes minores quinquaginta annis sacramento (abl.) rogaret, should administer the oath of allegiance to them, swear them in, ; so, rogare (aliquos) sacramento,; ; ; in a like sense: adigere sacramento aliquos,; ; ; ; : adigere aliquos sacramento Othonis,: Vitellii,: Vespasiani,: adigere aliquos sacramento in nomen senatūs,: sacramento aliquem tenere ... sacramento tenere,; cf.: secundo eum obliget militiae sacramento, quia, priore amisso, jure cum hostibus pugnare non poterat, (in which passage the primary jurid. signif. is alluded to): ex quibus (legionibus) aetate aut valetudine fessi sacramento solvebantur,: legionibus, quae sacramentum mutaverant, in paenitentiam conversis,i. e. had revolted,; cf.: paenitentia mutati sacramenti,: alicujus sacramentum exuere,: hoc sacramento (viz. in the service of Bacchus) initiatos juvenes milites faciendos censetis?.—
Transf., in gen., an oath, a solemn obligation or engagement (mostly post-Aug.): ut sacramento contendas mea non esse,: non ego perfidum Dixi sacramentum: ibimus, ibimus, etc.,: in verba Eumolpi sacramentum juravimus,: amicitiae sacramentum delevi,: sacramento quodam nexi,: se sacramento obstringere, ne, etc., (97), 7: si quod inesset mutis animalibus tacitum ac naturale sacramentum,.—
In eccl. and late Lat., something to be kept sacred.
A secret: sacramentum regis abscondere,.—
The gospel revelation: nolite verba, cum sacramentum meum Erit canendum, providenter quaerere, Prud. στεφ. 10,15.—
A mystery: sacramentum stellarum,: pietatis,; ; Aug. de Agone Christi, 24.—
A sacrament: signa, cum ad res divinas pertinent, sacramenta appellantur,: baptismi,: sanguinis Christi,: (matrimonii),.—
The office of the ministry: Athanasium episcopum... coctus in unum quaesitus (synodus ut appellant) removit a sacramento quod obtinebat,.

Meton., fixed or decreed as inviolable, sacred, inviolable, sacrosanct: ipsis quoque tribunis (plur.), ut sacrosancti viderentur (cujus rei prope jam memoria aboleverat), relatis quibusdam ex magno intervallo caerimoniis, renovarunt; et cum religione inviolatos eos, tum lege etiam fecerunt, sanciendo: ut qui tribunis plebis aedilibus, judicibus, decemviris nocuisset, ejus caput Jovi sacrum esset, etc. Hac lege juris interpretes negant quemquam sacrosanctum esse, sed cum quid eorum cuiquam nocuerit, id sacrum sanciri: itaque aedilem prehendi ducique a majoribus magistratibus: quod etsi non jure fiat (noceri enim ei, cui hac lege non liceat), tamen argumentum esse, non haberi pro sacro sanctoque aedilem; tribunos vetere jure jurando plebis, cum primum eam potestatem creavit, sacrosanctos esse,; cf.: sacrosanctum dicitur, quod jurejurando interposito est institutum, si quis id violasset, ut morte poenas penderet. Cujus generis sunt tribuni plebis aedilesque ejusdem ordinis, Müll.: sacrosanctum esse nihil potest, nisi quod populus plebesve sanxisset: deinde sanctiones sacrandae sunt genere ipso aut obtestatione legis aut poenā, cum caput ejus, qui contra fecerit, consecratur,: agi deinde de concordiā coeptum concessumque in condiciones, ut plebi sui magistratus essent sacrosancti,; so of the tribunes of the people,; (opp. profani); ; cf.: sacrosancta potestas (tribunorum, plur.), ; fin.: accusator, velut sacrosanctus erat,: SI QVID SACROSANCTVM EST, an old formula ap. : in vastatione omnium tuas possessiones sacrosanctas futuras putas?: colonos etiam maritimos, qui sacrosanctam vacationem dicebantur habere, dare milites cogebant, Drak.: Oedipodis ossa, honore arae decorata, quasi sacrosancta, —
Transf., in gen., most holy, most sacred, venerable (post-Aug.; freq. in the Christian writers): cujus (Rufi) mihi memoria sacrosancta est,; so, imago tua,: ista civitas (Roma),, p. 270: contemplatio conspectus tui (sc. episcopi),: de sacrosanctis ecclesiis,.
